name: Barbell Overhead Press
description: The barbell overhead press is a standing vertical pushing exercise in which a barbell is pressed from the front rack position to full overhead extension. It is the primary free-weight exercise for developing shoulder mass and pressing strength, and also trains the triceps and upper trapezius as significant synergists.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Hold the barbell in a front rack position at the upper chest with hands slightly wider than shoulder width. Elbows just in front of the bar, wrists straight.
execution.setup_instructions: Unrack the barbell from a squat rack set at upper chest height. Brace the core and squeeze the glutes before pressing to stabilize the spine.
steps: Take a breath and brace the core hard.
Press the bar straight up and slightly back as it passes the face, sliding the head back slightly to allow bar clearance.
Lock the bar out directly overhead with arms fully extended and biceps close to the ears.
Lower the bar under control back to the front rack position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before each press. Exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Pressing the bar forward instead of straight up and over the center of mass
Excessive lumbar hyperextension — maintain a braced, neutral lumbar curve
Not locking the bar out overhead fully
safety_considerations: If shoulder mobility limits an overhead lockout, work on thoracic extension and shoulder flexibility
Use a squat rack to unrack safely — do not clean from the floor for pressing sets
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full lockout overhead, bar returns to clavicle/upper chest level at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Press your head through your arms as the bar passes your face
Squeeze your glutes and abs hard — make your whole body a rigid pillar
